Login and session recovery.question: How should password and login-code authentication be presented?
Login and session recovery.answer: Use one /login page with password as the default and login code as an alternate mode; both converge on the same authoritative session restoration flow.
options_presented: One page, password default and login code alternate
One page, login code default and password alternate
Separate /login and /login/code pages

Login and session recovery.question: What should happen when an access token expires?
Login and session recovery.answer: Coalesce concurrent failures into one bounded refresh attempt. If refresh fails, clear the entire local session, redirect to login with a safe return target, and restore that target only after successful reauthentication.
options_presented: One automatic refresh then sign out with safe return target
No automatic refresh
Prompt the user before retry or sign-out

Login and session recovery.question: How should login-code request and verification failures be shown?
Login and session recovery.answer: Always use the same anti-enumeration acknowledgement regardless of account existence. Show server-policy resend countdown and attempt state without revealing identity existence; expiry or exhausted attempts require a new request.
options_presented: Generic acknowledgement plus server countdown and bounded attempt state
Generic acknowledgement with no countdown or attempt state
More detail for previously used devices

Login and session recovery.question: What should explicit logout affect?
Login and session recovery.answer: Logout is an explicit all-device global sign-out. The UI must disclose that scope, and a provider revocation failure must not be presented as successful logout after merely clearing local state.
options_presented: Explicit all-device logout
Current-browser-only logout
Current-browser logout plus a separate all-device action

Role registration and administrator revi.question: How should public registrants select a role?
Role registration and administrator revi.answer: Use the existing public registration system with explicit Student, Parent, and Teacher choices. The client and backend must never infer a role from email or a fallback default.
options_presented: Public Teacher registration followed by administrator review
Administrator directly creates Teacher accounts
Public Teacher registration with immediate Teacher authority

Role registration and administrator revi.question: How should legacy tutor and other non-authoritative role values be handled?
Role registration and administrator revi.answer: Teacher is the only active field and role term. Remove tutor from active types, fields, routes, aliases, and fallbacks. Historical tutor values are reconciliation inputs only; ordinary login rejects them without silently mapping or changing authority.
options_presented: Reject and route to controlled reconciliation
Automatically convert tutor to teacher
Enter a restricted Student fallback

Role registration and administrator revi.question: When does a Teacher registrant receive Teacher authority?
Role registration and administrator revi.answer: A Teacher registrant verifies their email and enters pending_review without Teacher privileges. Only an administrator approval may activate the authoritative teacher role.
options_presented: Email verification then pending administrator review
Administrator direct creation
Immediate activation after email verification

Role registration and administrator revi.question: What remains of the invitation and candidacy flows?
Role registration and administrator revi.answer: Remove the independent invitation, invitation-token consumption, and /teacher-access activation model. Pending or rejected Teacher registrants may authenticate only to a review-status experience and cannot access Teacher dashboards or student resources.
options_presented: Use existing registration plus administrator review and remove invitation activation
Keep invitation activation alongside public registration
Keep a separate Teacher candidacy page
